masterclass.name: MasterClass
masterclass.verdict: MasterClass's main membership is best treated as inspiration and craft insight from famous practitioners, not as a credential. Every plan unlocks the full library; you pay more only for extra simultaneous devices and offline viewing. Career-focused certificate courses are sold separately.
facts: Annual membership: Standard $10/mo, Plus $15/mo, Premium $20/mo, billed annually ($120, $180, $240 a year)
Not shown on the plan pages we checked
Standard 1; Plus up to 2 simultaneous streams; Premium up to 6

Main membership: not credential-focused. MasterClass Certificates are a separate paid product: 15–20-hour courses with a capstone project and shareable certificate, from $299 per course or a Certificates Annual Pass
Auto-renews; renewal notice sent 30 days before
masterclass.good: Curious learners who enjoy polished, documentary-style lessons and want breadth across cooking, writing, music, business and more. Plus or Premium suits households because of extra streams and profiles.
masterclass.bad: Anyone who needs graded work or step-by-step job skills from the main library. The upfront annual charge also makes it a poor fit for trying something for a month. MasterClass Certificates add credentials, but at extra cost (from $299 per course).
masterclass.take: Pick Standard if you watch alone online; Plus if two people share or you want offline downloads. Set a reminder before the renewal date, since the plan auto-renews.
sources: MasterClass Help: Subscription charge and renewal
MasterClass Certificates Help: what certificate courses include
MasterClass press release: certificate course with Microsoft (Apr 7, 2026; from $299)

updated.note: added MasterClass Certificates (separate certificate courses from $299, per MasterClass's 2026 announcements and help centre).

coursera.name: Coursera
coursera.verdict: Coursera is the strongest pick here if you want certificates from universities and companies. Coursera Plus bundles most of the catalog for one price.
facts: Coursera Plus $59/month or $399/year; single courses and programs $49–$79/month
Monthly Plus starts with a 7-day free trial
Annual Plus: refund request within 14 days of payment (certificates earned in that window are revoked)
Coursera, Inc., which has owned Udemy since May 11, 2026; the two platforms and their accounts still run separately
Free preview of the first module of most courses (this replaced free auditing in August 2025); some Community Impact courses are free in full; financial aid for eligible learners
coursera.good: Career changers and upskillers who want structured programs, graded assignments and recognisable certificates.
coursera.bad: Hobbyists who want short creative classes, and anyone who will study for only a few weeks at a time and forget to cancel.
coursera.take: At list prices, seven months of monthly Plus ($413) cost more than one year of annual Plus ($399), so choose annual only if you'll study most of the year. Annual Plus has a 14-day money-back guarantee.
sources: Coursera Help: Coursera Plus (trial and refund terms)
Coursera Blog: new course preview experience replaces audit (Aug 8, 2025)
Coursera Blog: what the Udemy combination means for Coursera learners

updated.note: free audit replaced by a free first-module preview (per Coursera's Aug 2025 announcement); added the May 2026 Udemy combination; re-checked Plus price, trial and refund terms on the Coursera Plus page.

skillshare.name: Skillshare
skillshare.verdict: Skillshare suits creatives who like short, hands-on classes with a project at the end. The web price is an annual plan charged upfront.
facts: Annual membership $167.88/yr (shown as $13.99/month) on the web pricing page
Via the Skillshare app through your app store
Certificates and badges to mark progress (per the pricing page); not presented as accredited credentials
7-day trial: one-time refund if requested within 48 hours of the charge and unused; no refunds for renewals; EU/UK 14-day cooling-off
skillshare.good: Illustrators, designers, photographers, crafters and freelancers who learn best by making something.
skillshare.bad: Learners who need accredited certificates or deep technical curricula.
skillshare.take: Use the trial to finish one or two class projects; if you do, the annual plan is reasonable value.
sources: Skillshare Help: What does Skillshare cost?
Skillshare Help: subscriptions, pricing and refunds

updated.note: re-checked the web price ($13.99/month, $167.88 billed annually) and certificate wording on Skillshare's pricing page; after the trial, the annual membership is billed in full.

udemy.name: Udemy
udemy.verdict: Udemy is the most flexible option: buy a single course and keep lifetime access, or subscribe to the Personal Plan for a curated collection. Refund rules differ sharply between the two.
facts: Individual course purchases, or Personal Plan subscription (monthly or annual access)
250,000+ courses overall (per Udemy); Personal Plan is a curated subset
Wholly owned by Coursera, Inc. since May 11, 2026; still a separate platform, catalog and account
May be offered to first-time Personal Plan subscribers

Eligible individual courses: 30-day refund policy (heavy use or repeat requests can be refused; some refunds are paid as Udemy credits). Subscriptions bought on Udemy.com: no refunds unless required by law
udemy.good: Self-directed learners who want one specific practical skill (a programming language, an exam, a software tool) at a low one-off cost.
udemy.bad: Anyone wanting consistent quality control: courses come from independent instructors, so check reviews and previews.
udemy.take: For one or two skills, buy courses individually and keep them. Consider the Personal Plan only if you will work through several courses within the subscription period.
sources: Coursera investor news: Coursera completes combination with Udemy (May 11, 2026)
Coursera Blog: what the Udemy combination means for Coursera learners

updated.note: added the May 2026 combination with Coursera and re-checked the refund policy on Udemy's help centre.

linkedin-learning.name: LinkedIn Learning
linkedin-learning.verdict: LinkedIn Learning is solid for business and software skills, but individuals can only get it through LinkedIn Premium or an employer, school or library.
facts: No standalone individual subscription; included with LinkedIn Premium. PCMag reports Premium Career at $39.99/month or $239.88/year
Premium free trial (typically one month), card required
Individual course purchases are not offered
linkedin-learning.good: Job seekers who also want Premium networking features, and anyone with free access via a library or employer.
linkedin-learning.bad: Learners who only want courses and do not value Premium's other features.
linkedin-learning.take: Check whether your public library or employer already gives you access before paying.
sources: LinkedIn Help: LinkedIn Learning subscription overview

edx.name: edX
edx.tagline: university courses with a free audit track
edx.verdict: edX lets you audit many university courses free, then pay to upgrade to a verified certificate. Prices are set per course.
facts: Per course; free audit track or paid verified track
Audit track: temporary access to course materials, no graded assignments or certificate
Verified certificate on the paid track
Varies by course; check the course's enrollment options
No trial needed: audit track is free
edx.good: Learners who want academic content and to try a course before paying for a certificate.
edx.bad: People wanting an all-you-can-learn subscription or creative hobby classes.
edx.take: Audit first; upgrade before the course's upgrade deadline only if you want the certificate. Until November 4, 2026, edX's FALL2026 code takes 15% off select verified courses and programs (our note on the edX fall offer).
sources: edX Help: What does it cost to take a course?

codecademy.name: Codecademy
codecademy.verdict: Codecademy is a beginner-friendly way to learn to code by writing code in the browser, with paid tiers for career paths and certifications.
facts: Free basic tier; Plus and Pro paid plans
$14.99/month billed annually or $29.99 billed monthly (per pricing page at time of check)
$19.99/month billed annually or $39.99 billed monthly; adds career paths, interview prep and certifications
Pro Student pricing for eligible students
No refunds on subscriptions (exceptions can be requested via support)
codecademy.good: Complete beginners and career switchers who want guided, hands-on practice.
codecademy.bad: Experienced developers wanting advanced, project-heavy material.
codecademy.take: Start on the free tier; upgrade to Pro only when you're ready for a full career path.

datacamp.name: DataCamp
datacamp.verdict: DataCamp focuses on data science, analytics and AI with short interactive exercises. Watch for frequent promotions on the annual plan.
facts: Free Basic tier (first chapter of every course) plus Premium subscription, billed monthly or yearly; Teams plans available
First chapter of every course free
$35/month billed monthly; $14/month billed annually (special price, regular $28) on Oct 15, 2026
Premium Student plan for eligible college students, described as over 50% off
Monthly subscribers can pause; yearly plans cannot be paused
Terms of Use: fees are non-refundable except as stated; no prorated refund on cancellation
datacamp.good: Analysts and aspiring data scientists learning Python, R, SQL and AI tools.
datacamp.take: Try the free first chapters, then buy annual Premium while a special price is running if you'll use it all year.

brilliant.name: Brilliant
brilliant.verdict: Brilliant teaches math, science and computer science through interactive problem solving rather than video lectures.
facts: Brilliant Premium: annual, monthly and family (up to 6 members) plans; limited free access
Individual $30/month or $20/month billed annually; Family (6 seats) $60/month or $40/month billed annually
Unlimited lessons and practice, AI tutor (Koji), ad-free, web/iOS/Android
Free plan with a daily lesson; K-12 teachers and students may qualify for free Premium
brilliant.good: Learners who enjoy puzzles and want to build quantitative intuition in short daily sessions.
brilliant.bad: People who want certificates or long-form lectures.
brilliant.take: A good daily habit tool; pair it with a course platform if you need credentials.
sources: Brilliant Help: How much does Premium cost?

domestika.name: Domestika
domestika.verdict: Domestika offers creative courses you can buy individually or access through the Domestika Plus subscription.
facts: Individual course purchases or Domestika Plus subscription
$33.90/month, or $164.50 for the first year; page states renewal after one year at the full $329
Annual Plus: 12 credits a year to keep courses forever; monthly: 1 credit a month
Certificate for each purchased course you complete
1,000+ courses free to watch with Plus
domestika.good: Creatives who want in-depth courses from working professionals, many originally produced in Spanish with subtitles.
domestika.bad: Learners seeking business, tech or accredited content.
domestika.take: Watch the renewal price: the annual Plus renewal shown on the page is about double the first-year price. Buy a single course if one topic interests you.

pluralsight.name: Pluralsight
pluralsight.tagline: tech skills with labs and skill assessments
pluralsight.verdict: Pluralsight is a technology-focused library with skill assessments, learning paths, certification prep and hands-on labs, sold in tiered plans.
facts: Individual plans: Core Tech, specialty plans (AI+, Cloud+, Data+, Security+) and Complete; monthly or yearly billing
10 days on any individual plan; includes a selection of hands-on labs, while offline downloads and full labs and sandboxes need a paid plan; converts to paid on day 11
Video courses, learning paths, labs, Skill IQ assessments, AI assistant, certification prep
Cloud/AI sandbox environments on Cloud+, AI+ and Complete
Billed yearly: Core Tech $21/mo, AI+/Cloud+/Data+/Security+ $24.50/mo, Complete $39/mo. Billed monthly: Core Tech $30, Complete $55
No refunds on individual subscriptions (cancel anytime)
pluralsight.good: IT pros and developers preparing for certifications or building cloud, security and data skills.
pluralsight.take: Start with Core Tech; only pay for Complete if you'll use the sandboxes.
sources: Pluralsight Help: Free trial for individuals

updated.note: free-trial details re-checked (a selection of labs is now included; converts to paid on day 11); refund policy re-checked and its help-center link updated after the old article moved.

udacity.name: Udacity
udacity.verdict: Udacity sells All Access to its whole catalog of Nanodegree programs and courses, aimed at job-ready tech skills. It is expensive at list price, so time your enrollment.
facts: All Access subscription: $249/month, or $846 upfront for four months (15% saving), then month-to-month
All Nanodegrees and courses while subscribed
udacity.good: Motivated learners who can finish a Nanodegree in a few focused months.
udacity.take: Use the four-month bundle only if you can commit the hours.

futurelearn.name: FutureLearn
futurelearn.verdict: FutureLearn offers short courses from universities and organisations; Unlimited gives a year of access to most of them.
facts: Unlimited annual subscription; individual upgrades also sold
$349.99/year list; $244.99 first-year offer shown on Oct 15, 2026
futurelearn.good: Learners who like short, structured university courses in health, teaching, psychology and business.
futurelearn.take: Buy Unlimited during an offer and note the renewal date.

khan-academy.name: Khan Academy
khan-academy.verdict: Khan Academy is a nonprofit offering its core library free, with no ads, from early maths to college-level subjects. Its AI tutor Khanmigo is a separate paid option for learners in some regions.
facts: AI tutor; free for teachers in many countries, paid for learners where offered
khan-academy.good: Students, parents and adults refreshing maths, science and test-prep fundamentals.
khan-academy.take: Start here before paying for any foundational course.
sources: Khan Academy Help: Does it cost money?
Khan Academy Blog: Khanmigo for teachers

great-courses-plus.name: The Great Courses Plus
great-courses-plus.verdict: The Great Courses Plus (the service formerly called Wondrium) streams long-form lecture courses in history, science, philosophy and more.
facts: Streaming subscription with several billing periods
Monthly, quarterly and annual plans; the prices we saw were in EUR only, so check the plans page for US pricing
Long-form lectures by professors and experts
No refund for early termination (per plans page)
great-courses-plus.good: Lifelong learners who enjoy in-depth lectures.
great-courses-plus.take: Check the plans page for current offers before subscribing.

babbel.name: Babbel
babbel.verdict: Babbel teaches languages through structured, conversation-focused lessons, sold as subscriptions with a lifetime option.
facts: Subscriptions of several lengths, plus a lifetime option
$17.95 for 1 month; $45.75 per 3 months; $80.70 per 6 months; $107.40 per 12 months; Lifetime $299.99
Short lessons focused on practical conversation
babbel.good: Beginners who want structured grammar and dialogue.
babbel.take: Longer plans cost less per month; compare with Duolingo's free tier first.

duolingo.name: Duolingo
duolingo.verdict: Duolingo is free to use with ads and limits; Super Duolingo removes ads and adds unlimited hearts and extra practice.
facts: Free with ads; Super Duolingo subscription
No ads, unlimited hearts, personalised practice, mistakes review
No (Duolingo English Test is a separate product)
Duolingo terms: payments nonrefundable unless required by law; app-store refunds via Apple or Google
duolingo.good: Anyone building a daily language habit on a budget.
duolingo.take: Use the free tier first; upgrade only if limits annoy you.

alison.name: Alison
alison.verdict: Alison courses are free to study and finish. You can download a free learner record; formal digital or printed certificates are optional purchases.
facts: Free learner record; certificates sold in Alison's shop, some courses include free digital ones
alison.good: Budget learners who want proof of completion.
alison.take: Good free starting point; pay only if an employer values the certificate.
sources: Alison Help: Is Alison really free?
Alison Help: How do I get my certificate?
news: Oct 16, 2026: Alison adds free in-browser Python coding labs

teachable.name: Teachable
teachable.tagline: platform for selling your own course
teachable.verdict: Teachable is a platform for creators to sell courses. For learners, courses hosted on Teachable are run by independent creators, so quality and refund terms vary by school.
facts: Creator plans: Starter, Builder, Growth, Custom; monthly or annual
Teachable lists a platform transaction fee on Starter only; payment processing fees apply
Each school sets its own prices and refund policy
teachable.good: Creators who want to sell courses under their own brand.
teachable.take: Learners: check each school's refund policy before buying.

rosetta-stone.name: Rosetta Stone
rosetta-stone.verdict: Rosetta Stone teaches languages through immersion and offers subscriptions and a one-time lifetime option covering all its languages.
facts: Access while the product and services remain available and supported
rosetta-stone.good: Learners who like immersion and want many languages.
rosetta-stone.take: Read the lifetime terms before buying.
